verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium, from the content step. If the site team fills the seed drafts from READMEs, the page states 'works with / produces / limitations' under the author's name without the author having confirmed them (e.g. 'accepts CellProfiler output' is not in the CellTracksColab README). A visible 'Not stated by the author' on every page for three fields is noisy, and for game/utility apps it would be wrong.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Build it, smaller. (1) Schema: optional `inputs`, `outputs`, `limitations`, each 1-6 plain-text items of 5-160 characters, with the descriptions saying 'summary, not README copy; use docs_url for the rest'. The schema is additionalProperties:false, so publish the site schema first, then the initialiser (LabConstrictor_streamlit schemas copy, app_manifest.py, manifest_form.py), then the apps. (2) Render a 'Works with' and a 'Produces' block under the header, and 'Limitations' under 'Using it', only when present, in a new module (pages_apps.py is 208/300 lines). Read the fields with `in` or optional_list, no .get default. (3) For kinds analysis, segmentation and simulation only, add one WARNING per app in catalogue.resolve warnings (never unlist, same as the icon precedent) when inputs or outputs are missing, and show one muted line 'Input and output formats: not stated by the author'. Do not show Not stated for limitations or for game/training/utility/testing apps. (4) Seed drafts: copy only statements that are literally in the README, marked as drafts for the owners to confirm (the seed header already says DRAFT). Add the pattern to DESIGN.md first, and tests for present, absent and over-length (cap) cases. Do not add a separate example_data field (see G4).

verdicts.misleading_risk: High if done as proposed. A `platforms` field makes the author state twice what the release already shows, and a site-written 'Intel Macs: not supported' line drawn from a README sentence is the site inferring support. 'Experimental in napari' is accurate only if tied to the host project status file; a hand-written label would repeat the current inconsistency. The VLab4Mic napari/Fiji claim is currently an unverified statement on the live page.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Split into four items, in this order. (a) Installers: fix at the source. The Intel .pkg exists only because the template workflow (release_constructor.yml:93-94, copied into each app and refreshed by sync_template.yml) builds macos-15-intel unconditionally. Ask for an opt-out in the template and have GuessTheCondition and Playground stop publishing the x86_64 pkg; the site then derives the truth from the release assets, with no new field. Only if owners must keep the asset, add an optional manifest field naming the unsupported platforms (e.g. `unsupported: [macos-x86_64]`), shown as an explicit line and never hidden. (b) Host wording: one function used by cards.host_badge/host_chip (cards.py:68-71) and details_list 'Works in' (pages_apps.py:170-173). Take the label from the matching host project's `status` in build/sources/*/docs/labconstrictor-project.yaml, for example 'Experimental in napari' when it says Experimental; all three (napari, Fiji, QuPath) currently say Experimental. Keep 'Soon' only for a status that means not yet usable, and add no status to hosts.yaml by hand. Update the AGENTS.md sentence 'Host chips ... (Soon in ...)' and DESIGN.md Badges in the same change. (c) VLab4Mic: drop `napari, fiji` from the seed draft hosts and the 'Two of its tools also run in Napari and Fiji' sentence until the maintainers confirm; nothing in the local clone supports it. (d) Architecture: print the arch from assets[].arch on every tile (derivable, S). Skip RAM/disk fields; hardware needs go in `limitations` (G1) only if the author states them.
